OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 9, 2026 (11:14 a.m. EST audit)

STATUS: Direct, time-stamped Diversion Canal discharge, direction and velocity NOT independently verified. Santee Cooper's operational feed states updated November 9, but its latest DAILY lake elevations and facility discharge entries are dated November 8; observation times are not specified. November 9 daily elevations are not yet published in that table. No current measured canal-flow rate or qualitative strength classification is supported.

OPERATOR-REPORTED LAKE ELEVATIONS (feet, individual measurement times unspecified): November 8 Lake Marion 74.26, Lake Moultrie 74.17, nominal difference 0.09 ft (Marion higher). November 7 Marion 74.25, Moultrie 74.18, difference 0.07 ft. November 6 Marion 74.26, Moultrie 74.17, difference 0.09 ft. From November 7 to November 8 Marion rose 0.01 ft, Moultrie fell 0.01 ft, and the nominal difference widened by 0.02 ft, from 0.07 to 0.09 ft. These are operator-published daily numbers, not synchronized readings. The USGS Elloree and Pinopolis monitoring pages returned HTTP 403 during this audit, so independent observation timestamps and vertical-datum comparability could not be confirmed. Treat nominal differences as provisional, NOT independently verified simultaneous hydraulic head.

HYDRO OPERATIONS (operator feed updated November 9; tentative, subject to change): Monday November 9 Jefferies Hydro scheduled 6 a.m.–8 p.m.; Tuesday November 10 Jefferies scheduled 6 a.m.–10 p.m. St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled to run on either date. The November 8 daily facility table lists Jefferies Hydro 3,608, St. Stephen Hydro 0, Spillway Hydro 8, Spilling 770 (units not independently established here); November 7 lists Jefferies 4,004 and St. Stephen 0. These are facility table entries, NOT Diversion Canal flow measurements. Neither a Jefferies schedule nor a St. Stephen schedule proves present canal discharge.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL, NOT MEASURED: If the operator's lake elevations use comparable vertical datums and broadly contemporaneous observations, the nominal Marion-above-Moultrie elevation is consistent with a potential hydraulic gradient from Marion toward Moultrie. The latest nominal difference increased, but this alone does not establish actual canal flow, velocity, local direction or strength. Santee Cooper states that adjusting Lake Moultrie storage through St. Stephen operations changes the lake-to-lake head and diversion flows; that is general operating context, not today's direct canal observation. Classification: CURRENT CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED; no defensible strength estimate.

Replaces November 8 assessment.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
